title: Consulting the Digital Doctor: Efficacy of ChatGPT-3.5 in Answering Questions Related to Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care
authors: Rachel N. Rohrich, Karen R. Li, Christian X. Lava, Isabel Snee, Sami Alahmadi, Richard C. Youn, John S. Steinberg, Jayson N. Atves, Christopher E. Attinger, Karen K. Evans

reading.body:
ChatGPT-3.5 answered diabetic foot ulcer questions with a mean accuracy of 8.7 out of 10, but three of eleven responses contained incorrect information and ten omitted key details.

The pattern is a tool that is broadly right and specifically unreliable. Reviewers rated danger low at 2.2 out of 10 and praised simplicity in all eleven cases, so the failure mode is not alarming nonsense. It is confident, readable answers that drop the details a patient would need, including deep vein thrombosis symptoms and comorbidities affecting limb salvage. Ten of eleven responses had at least one such gap.

That matters for AI because the constraint here is not compute, buildings, or power. It is the quality of the model's medical knowledge and the reading level of its output, which averaged an 11.9 grade level against an average American adult well below that. A model can be cheap to run and still be the wrong instrument for a clinical question.

The data covers eleven questions, four surgeon reviewers, and one model version, ChatGPT-3.5, queried in December 2023. It does not measure newer models, real patient outcomes, or whether patients act on the errors. It supports treating the chatbot as a supplement to a clinician, not a replacement.

explain_beginner: This study asked whether a popular AI chatbot gives good answers about caring for diabetic foot ulcers, which are serious wounds linked to diabetes. Doctors asked the chatbot 11 common questions and then rated the replies. The answers were mostly accurate and easy to understand, but some contained wrong information, and most left out important details. The chatbot also wrote at a reading level too hard for many adults. The takeaway is that AI can help patients learn general information and feel more involved in their care, but it should not replace a doctor, and patients should check important advice with their medical team.
explain_business: This evaluation of ChatGPT-3.5 for diabetic foot ulcer questions shows the tool can deliver generally accurate, understandable information but also produces occasional errors and frequent omissions, and it writes at a reading level above the average American adult. For healthcare organizations, this signals both opportunity and risk. Patients will use AI for wound care guidance, so leaders should decide how to guide that use, for example by offering vetted educational content, training staff to discuss AI limits, and monitoring for misinformation. The findings support treating AI as a supplement to clinical care rather than a trusted standalone source, and they inform investments in patient education and safety protocols.
explain_practitioner: Researchers queried ChatGPT-3.5 with 11 frequently asked diabetic foot ulcer care questions in December 2023, covering wound care, concerning symptoms, and surgical management. Four plastic surgeons rated each response on a 10-point scale for accuracy, comprehensiveness, and danger, and gave qualitative feedback. Ten readability indexes assessed reading level. Mean scores were 8.7 for accuracy, 8.0 for comprehensiveness, and 2.2 for danger. Responses averaged an 11.9 grade level. Reviewers praised simplicity in all 11 cases and general information value in 4. Three responses contained incorrect information, and 10 omitted key details such as deep vein thrombosis symptoms and comorbidities affecting limb salvage.
